# Ternuxx

**Repository:** [`soobujmiah/ternuxx`](https://github.com/soobujmiah/ternuxx). Use ./tx from a source checkout or the installed tx command.

**বাংলা:** Pocket-এ mobile workstation তৈরির স্বাধীন project। Native Termux layer compatible tools ও Android-facing integration-এর সুযোগ দেবে; বিদ্যমান Ternux Debian PRoot layer Linux desktop, established workload ও configured GPU path দেবে। Hybrid mode দুটিকে নিরাপদ handoff দিয়ে এক workstation-এ যুক্ত করবে।

**English:** I want my phone to be a workstation I can carry in my pocket. I want native Termux and my existing Ternux PRoot setup to work together, so I can use each where it fits. Read [what I have in mind](docs/PRODUCT-VISION.md).

## Quick start

Run these commands in Native Termux from the checkout:

```sh
./tx help
./tx info
./tx tui
./tx web
```

`./tx mng center` opens the Native GTK management app when the desktop and GTK dependencies are installed. `./tx db` opens the existing Debian PRoot shell. `./tx pgui` opens the existing Debian XFCE desktop: standalone on `:0` when Native GUI is stopped, or nested through Xephyr on `:2` inside Native `:1`. Installed Debian GUI apps are auto-listed in a separate Native XFCE **PRoot Apps** menu. Refresh after changing guest apps with `./tx mng papps sync`; launch by menu or `./tx mng app launch --desktop-id APP.desktop`. The four management clients use the shared service, though feature coverage still differs by client.

## Planned use and current workstation boundary

- **Native mode:** Native Termux is the Ternuxx host and management authority. CPU is the baseline. The saved Native selection points to the locally staged KGSL/Freedreno candidate; current `:1` status reports Adreno 825 with `Accelerated: yes`, and bounded GL workloads rendered successfully. Native Vulkan only enumerates the device, and no Vulkan draw or inference workload has been verified. A clean install uses stock Mesa until a provider installer exists.
- **Debian PRoot:** Ternuxx uses the existing Debian rootfs through typed `proot-distro` operations. `tx pgui` now supervises a standalone XFCE desktop on `:0` when Native GUI is stopped, or runs a full nested Debian desktop through Xephyr `:2` inside Native `:1`. Device checks verified the standalone `:0` Zink/Turnip renderer and a 693-frame Debian GLX draw on Native `:1`; the nested Xephyr `:2` desktop reports DRI3 unavailable and GLX draw at zero frames; its Zink/Turnip GLES context does not verify a draw or presentation. Authenticated Native PulseAudio was reachable on both routes. The existing rootfs is recorded in Ternuxx private state. A separate preview-bound fresh Debian Trixie provisioner exists, but it has fixture evidence only and refuses an existing rootfs; migration of the current guest's packages/configuration remains unimplemented. General PRoot attach/detach and arbitrary session stop ownership remain unqualified.
- **Hybrid handoff:** Ternuxx routes selected guest applications to its verified Native :1 display and host audio endpoint. VirGL remains a separate preserved option but is not active/renderer-qualified in this snapshot.

The separate Ternux project remains independent and reference-only. Ternuxx does not require its CLI or state files. Existing Debian user data, packages, GPU setup, db/launcher aliases, x.sh, xgo, and killx are preserved; any targeted guest config adaptation requires a bounded impact assessment and recovery plan. Native Bionic libraries are not copied into Debian glibc paths. NPU execution remains unverified.


## PRoot Apps menu

Native XFCE gets a separate **PRoot Apps** category built from the visible application entries installed in the existing Debian guest. Ternuxx refreshes these launchers when its Native desktop starts; after adding or removing a Debian app while the desktop is open, run `./tx mng papps sync`. Each menu item goes through the shared management service and opens the matching guest desktop entry. Unrecognized or shell-command entries are skipped, and conflicting user-owned launchers are preserved.

## Existing Debian setup

Inspect the Ternuxx provider record with `./tx proot setup status`. If this checkout has not recorded the existing Debian rootfs, run `./tx proot setup adopt-preview --user NAME`, review the identified guest and plan, then apply that exact plan with `./tx proot setup adopt --user NAME --yes --plan-id ID`. Adoption records the rootfs identity in private Native state and does not modify Debian. It does not yet install packages, migrate guest configuration, reproduce a fresh Debian setup, or remove the legacy Ternux CLI. See [the setup status and limits](docs/INSTALLATION.md#existing-debian-provider).

## Development notes

The install command uses a preview-first Termux APT transaction and persists full dependency plans under private Ternuxx state. The base Native workstation set includes `proot-distro` plus the desktop host packages; the versioned Debian profile now includes `xserver-xephyr` for nested GUI support. The base manager install never installs or replaces a Debian rootfs. A separate fresh Debian installer is preview-bound and fixture-tested, but has not been applied to a clean profile; existing `debian` is refused. The historical 2026-10-18 XFCE transaction is recorded with all 77 package versions in P2 evidence. P2 is complete for the recorded target. P3 remains active. Ternuxx now runs its own bounded, read-only Debian display/audio/renderer verification and passes explicit Native display, cookie-authenticated PulseAudio, and Zink/Turnip settings to its direct PRoot commands; it does not invoke the separate Ternux CLI. Headless fixtures and a foreground interactive login have passed live ownership checks; detach/reattach, exact managed stop of a running login, production boot, and shared-rootfs concurrency remain unqualified. The stock Native Vulkan route previously rejected Adreno 825; the selected experimental candidate now renders a bounded 120-frame `vkcube` workload on `:1`, with device identity matched to enumeration. Native GLES verification through the shared manager rendered a 1280x720 shader pbuffer workload at 219.47 frames/sec on Adreno 825. That is synthetic off-screen throughput, not screen FPS. Debian GLX on Native display :1 rendered 580 bounded frames through Zink/Turnip in the latest recheck; full nested Xephyr :2 still has no verified draw. Ordinary app API-aware fallback, clean-install driver reproduction, nested Xephyr presentation, VirGL guest renderer, inference workload, and NPU runtime/workload remain unqualified.

See [PRoot session lifecycle](docs/architecture/PROOT-SESSIONS.md), [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Native/PRoot integration](docs/HYBRID-INTEGRATION.md), [Native Wine and Hangover](docs/WINE-NATIVE.md), [workload optimization](docs/OPTIMIZATION.md), [documentation and SKB sync](docs/KNOWLEDGE-SYNC.md), [installation status](docs/INSTALLATION.md), and [AI assistant instructions](AI_ASSISTANT.md). The repository's [SKB knowledge-sync pointer](SKB_KNOWLEDGE_SYNC.md) explains internal knowledge return and the separate deterministic-state workflow.

For current CPU/GPU/NPU inference status, evidence requirements, compatibility, and benchmark methodology, see [testing and acceleration evidence](docs/testing/README.md). Ternuxx itself has no implemented inference backend or benchmark; the separate Ternux repository documents optional CPU/Vulkan llama.cpp and experimental SM8735 HTP extensions whose installed state and Ternuxx integration remain unverified.

The accepted product direction has four clients—CLI, interactive Terminal/TUI, Web UI, and Native graphical UI—calling one shared management service and operation contract. Implementation remains partial: the CLI/service foundation, selected X11 shortcut manager, catalog-backed TUI and Web Console, and installed GTK4 Management Center exist. Current actions and gaps are tracked in the [capability matrix](docs/architecture/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md). The [unified workstation architecture](docs/architecture/UNIFIED-WORKSTATION.md) and [management API contract](docs/architecture/MANAGEMENT-API.md) distinguish implemented behavior from planned clients and adapters; no model manager or AI gateway is implemented.

The [Master initiative Phase 0 audit](docs/evidence/PHASE-0-MASTER-AUDIT.md) records the current repository/device baseline, existing Termux integrations, the independent Ternux provider boundary, GUI feasibility, risks, and phase-mapped gaps. It is read-only audit evidence, not a claim that product acceptance tests have passed.

### Ternuxx Management Center

Use `tx tui` for the keyboard interface, `tx web` for the authenticated loopback Web Console, and `tx mng center install` followed by `tx mng center` for the separate Native Termux GTK4 application. They read the same catalog and call the shared management service, while each client exposes only its implemented and authorized actions. The Web Console provides confirmed desktop lifecycle, graphics status/verification and Native backend selection, GUI Activity/focus policy, managed SSH 8023 preview/confirmation, Cron status/job reads, preview-confirmed create/update/remove, and execution-history reads, timezone status/zone listing, named PRoot app launch with per-app confirmation, and preview-confirmed single-shortcut add/remove. The TUI additionally offers named PRoot app launch and preview-confirmed shortcut add/remove, Native graphics selection/verification, monitoring policy, Cron job listing and guided create/update/remove plus execution history, recovery history, and confirmed Ternuxx timezone preference. GTK provides confirmed desktop start/stop, graphics status/OpenGL/GLES/Vulkan verification and Native backend selection, managed SSH 8023 preview/confirmation, monitoring policy, Cron saved-job and execution-history reads plus guided create/rename/remove, recovery history, a Ternuxx timezone preference form, named PRoot app launch, and preview-confirmed single-shortcut add/remove. Current per-client limits are recorded in the [capability matrix](docs/architecture/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md); support in the shared catalog alone does not mean every client can perform that operation. The TUI uses a centered three-line brand header, wraps long content on narrow terminals, keeps a uniform text size, and colors resource status and footer hints by type; it also shows category availability counts, search, and selected-resource actions. In the Web Console, Recent management activity loads the bounded recovery operation history; raw responses remain under Technical API response. The management API exposes only bounded, fixed-path Ternuxx logs: Native XFCE desktop output, the Cron scheduler, and the management audit trail; the desktop log may include app output. The Activity monitoring policy is shown only with its Android Activity resource; Linux GUI health remains a separate status check.

Cron definitions now have a typed, persistent registry and deterministic schedule previews under `tx mng cron`; the lease-guarded scheduler runtime is available for explicit start but is not installed in boot or started by default. Production retry, cancellation, non-skip missed-run and boot/recovery delivery remain unqualified. The management clients keep Android Activity/focus monitoring disabled by default; status reads do not launch Termux:X11 or poll Android focus. The Web listener stays loopback-only and browser writes use a one-time terminal secret, scoped capabilities, CSRF proof, confirmation, and durable idempotency. Port 8022 is read-only and externally managed. CLI/TUI/Web/GTK expose bounded Ternuxx desktop, scheduler, and management-audit log tails; the desktop tail may contain XFCE app output, while arbitrary paths and Android-global logs are not exposed. The clients still do not expose all local CLI/service actions: interactive PRoot login and session lifecycle remain limited, alongside broad shortcut synchronization, boot changes, backup/restore writes, Cron scheduler lifecycle, SSH deployment/rollback, and operation-progress tracking. Web intentionally has no timezone mutation scope; TUI and GTK update the Ternuxx scheduling preference without changing Android system time. The shared recovery journal is available in the TUI, Web, and GTK as history. Resource cards identify planned or unavailable work instead of simulating it. The Native GTK app is installed from repository source with a source/installed hash record. Launching it creates an X11 window and may take desktop focus.

### Managed SSH service deployment

The native managed SSH service on port 8023 has a preview-first run-definition deployment workflow. `tx ssh deploy` shows a hash-bound diff; apply requires `--yes --plan-id` from that preview. Deployment preserves the running process and never restarts the service. Snapshot rollback is also preview-first (`tx ssh deploy-rollback-preview --operation-id ID`, then `tx ssh deploy-rollback --operation-id ID --yes --plan-id PLAN`). The separate owner-started 8022 development channel is not managed by this workflow. Process ownership/reboot qualification limitations are recorded in [8023 evidence](docs/evidence/2026-10-18-8023-reconciliation.md); see the [qualification plan](docs/testing/8023-deployment-and-lifecycle.md).
